newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Latest results show Armenia president poll winner.
newsitem.headline: Latest results show Armenia president poll winner.

text.p: Preliminary final results issued by Armenia's Central Electoral Commission on Wednesday showed that President Levon Ter-Petrosyan had won a second term.
Central Elections Commission chief Khachik Bezirjyan said Ter-Petrosyan got 52.09 percent of the votes cast against 41.07 for his main rival Vazgen Manukyan.
The turnout in Sunday's contest was 58.7 percent of the 2.2 million electorate with votes from all 11 regions counted.
Communist party candidate Sergei Badalyan got 6.21 percent and the fourth candidate, Ashot Manucharyan got 0.63 percent.

Ter-Petrosyan, leader of the small Caucasus country of 3.5 million since independence in 1991, needed a simple majority to avoid a second round runoff, but observers said numerous incidences of obvious fraud were committed by his supporters.
Supporters of Manukyan, Ter-Petrosyan's former prime minister turned bitter rival, have contested the result and held huge rallies every day since the vote.
Final official results must be released by Sunday.
